sentence_stem: Had the storm arrived an hour earlier,
correct_completion: the entire expedition would have been abandoned.
full_sentence: Had the storm arrived an hour earlier, the entire expedition would have been abandoned.
acceptable_variants: the whole mission would have been called off.
the team would have turned back immediately.

options.text: the expedition will be abandoned tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense does not match the hypothetical past set up by the inverted 'Had ... arrived' clause.

options.text: the expedition had been abandoned already.
options.why_wrong: The past perfect reports a completed fact. The sentence needs 'would have' plus a past participle to express the imagined result.

options.text: the entire expedition would have been abandoned.
so we would abandon it now.
options.why_wrong: The word 'so' signals a real cause, and the present conditional does not match the past condition introduced by 'Had'.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: An inverted third conditional drops 'if' and moves 'had' to the front of the clause, so the main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle to describe the imagined result. Polish speakers often try to mark the conditional inside the main clause with a single simple verb form, but English requires the 'would have' structure to link back to the past condition.
translation: Gdyby burza nadeszła godzinę wcześniej, cała wyprawa zostałaby porzucona.
